title: Tool invocation regression detector and shadow mitigator
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Build a runtime component that detects regressions in tool-invocation behavior (structured outputs and function-call contracts) during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts and automatically mitigates via traffic steering or rollback. The detector must compare live candidate behavior to the incumbent across multiple dimensions (call presence, argument shapes, return structure, confidence distribution) and surface deterministic signals suitable for automated policy actions.
background: Recent rollouts exposed latent incompatibilities where new model variants added optional parameters or reordered structured fields, causing downstream tool failures in production integrations. Current rollout guards focus on coarse schema diffs or synthetic fuzzing; we need a lightweight live detector that runs on shadow traffic and produces a compact regression score for automated mitigations and operator investigation.
proposal: Implement a probabilistic regression detector that computes per-invocation 'compatibility fingerprints' for both incumbent and candidate variants. Fingerprints encode: invocation presence (binary), function name hashes, arity and named-argument sets, argument types and shallow shapes, response top-level keys and type signatures, and a tokenized similarity score for string-typed fields. Compare candidate vs incumbent over a sliding window and compute weighted deltas to produce: (1) compatibility_rate, (2) structural_break_fraction, (3) invocation_parity_mismatch. Wire the detector into existing rollout controller: when thresholds breach, controller will first shift shadow traffic to 100% sink and notify on-call; for higher severity triggers, execute an auto-unwind rollback policy. Include operator-configurable thresholds and a dry-run mode for 2 cycles.
implementation_notes: Detector lives in runtime-observability service as an inline probe with <1ms p50 overhead per call when sampling 10% of traffic
Use protobuf-lite canonicalizer to normalize argument order for deterministic fingerprinting
Expose a compact telemetry vector to reduce metrics cardinality: {invocation_present, function_hash, shape_signature_hash, similarity_bucket}
Initial rollout uses shadow-traffic only; periodic A/B gating will be enabled after 2 weeks of shadow validation
progress_updates: 2026-01-27: Ticket created after postmortem for registry-incident-2026-01; design kickoff with product and SRE
2026-02-10: Prototype fingerprint library implemented; validated on historical traces from three customers with known regressions
2026-02-22: Review with Product: require operator thresholds and manual veto before auto-rollback for P1 customers
2026-03-03: PR #3078 opened (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3078) with detector core and sampling hooks
2026-03-10: Integration tests added; shadow sink and telemetry dashboards seeded; running internal canary on dev cluster
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint canonicalization across edge cases (reordered args, missing optional keys, nested empty arrays)
Synthetic regression suite that injects argument renames and added required fields and verifies detector delta crosses threshold
Integration test that runs candidate and incumbent against shared prompt set and asserts compatibility_rate >= 99% for safe rollouts
E2E test for auto-unwind that simulates severe structural_break_fraction and validates controller moves traffic to fallback model and creates an incident ticket
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow-only): enable detector for 1% shadow traffic across internal customers for 7 days; collect baseline metrics
Phase 1 (expanded shadow): 10% shadow traffic for 14 days; surface weekly compatibility reports to owners
Phase 2 (canary): 0.5% routed candidate traffic with detector gating; if no critical triggers for 72h, increase to 5%
Phase 3 (A/B): run 50/50 for a subset of low-impact customers with manual veto; enable auto-unwind for customers who opt-in
Fail-safe: Immediate sink of candidate traffic and notify on-call if compatibility_rate < 95% and structural_break_fraction > 1% in a 30m window
acceptance_criteria: Detector deployed to canary environment and adds <3% p99 latency to inference path when sampling at production rates
Detector correctly identifies 5 historical regression cases from past incidents and produces compatible scores
Rollout controller honors detector signals and executes traffic-sink and auto-unwind according to policy in integration tests
Dashboard visualizes compatibility metrics and links to example failing invocations for operator triage
blockers: Finalize threshold recommendations with Solutions team for enterprise customers
KMS token for telemetry export to external partner dashboards needs approval
follow_ups: Automated remediation playbooks per customer tier (P0/P1 opt-in) to define whether auto-unwind is allowed
Add a lightweight explainability UI that surfaces which fields caused structural_break_fraction to spike
Extend detector to metricize soft-contract changes (additive optional fields) vs hard-breaks
